text: *edited with new findings regarding complaint* If using mouse and not keyboard it always picks the middle power up instead of the one I selected, you have to use the wasd keys to navigate upgrade choices and then submit using spacebar. What a massive disappointment. Seriously, I expected way better than this.

There's a playable game here, but it's undercooked.

It looks and sounds like an old flash game from the 2000s, but if you played many of those, remember that there were plenty of rancid shovelware-tier ones. Even the good ones were often merely enjoyable because they were **free** and sort of portable, being playable on nearly any PC with an internet connection.
The sound design in particular is pretty bad, in my opinion. Some things you'd expect to have sounds (like the landlord exploding upon a win) simply don't. The sounds you do hear are either pretty generic or actively unpleasant-- in particular, the customers. Every single one makes the same pitched-up annoying "numnumnum" on eating or an obnoxious, childish growl if they don't get their food fast enough, which can happen often due to the food being served on a conveyer belt (meaning it might be eaten too fast by customers on the left side, although you have some ways to influence this). Maybe giving the various customers specific sound queues in addition to gameplay quirks (like the one that eats poop) would really benefit the experience.
It's not actively bad, visually, although the customers all grow and shrink excessively in some kind of awkward "breathing" pseudo-animation. Each one has a sprite for idling, eating, and getting impatient, which is good enough. I do love the giant goblin+baby army boss.
Gameplay-wise, it's as unpolished as you'd expect from a fresh Early Access roguelike, but to be fair, I could on

Update June 2026:
So after some updates i thought to try it again and see if it became more complex and challenging.
It got a tad bit more challenging but still not a lot.
I did two more runs and i beat second difficulty first try, third difficulty second try, but i wasnt tryharding at all.
I like the new perks etc, but overall it didnt get enough variation or stuff to keep me playing.
Endless Mode is pointless because i scaled so strong that i couldnt even pick any more upgrades.
Theres also not a lot to do in this kitchen, its all pretty basic and im not seeing the major differences between the first kitchen and the second water based one.

I couldnt even tell whats missing here. But to me it seems like the basic formula works well, but is still lacking something to make it fun.
Whether its the dishes being too sub complex or the customers being too sub complex, i dont know.
Maybe i need more cooking minigames to be busy, maybe perks feel too strong and onesided.
I cant tell.
But it feels a lot like a Mobile Game, so i wasnt really surprised to see it is one.

What i might like to see:
More modes with challenges, more complex gadgets, gadget meta progression instead of purchasing perks (like leveling/improving my rice cooker), more substantial and interesting perks, that dont outright eliminate gameplay elements.



Tried it and went through it pretty easily.
I didnt reach max difficulty in my playtime, but went through the first two with only doing the same dish constantly

While I enjoyed the game, there's VERY little content so far in the game, and they've added virtually nothing to the game since it released in February (They've added a single practically cosmetic customer to the game). The first "major" update they've announced still isn't coming until June 18th. This is not a big nor technical game, and is a two person dev team, 4 months for 1 update in an EA game is REALLY slow and is NOT encouraging for this game. I foresee it abandoned or with a low player count within the year.
Game doesn't seem to be going anywhere, not interested
If you want a mobile game, that reminds you of the glory days of free flash games running on miniclip.com, this is perfect for you. sadly, not for me.
